title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025–2026)

The fourth generation continued the Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming across multiple releases spanning late 2025 and 2026. Key models:

| Model | ID | Released | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Oct 2025 | Fastest/cheapest Claude 4 |
| Sonnet 4.5 | `claude-sonnet-4-5` | Sep 2025 | Best for complex agents and coding |
| Sonnet 4.6 | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Feb 2026 | Improved agentic search; 1M context GA |
| Opus 4.7 | `claude-opus-4-7` | Apr 2026 | New tokenizer; xhigh effort; 2576px images |
| Opus 4.8 | `claude-opus-4-8` | May 2026 | 1M context default; 128K output; smarter adaptive thinking |

Claude 4 models show substantial improvements in agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction following precision.

### Claude Opus 4.7 (April 16, 2026)

Introduced a **new tokenizer** — the same text produces roughly 30% more tokens compared to models before Opus 4.7. Other additions: `xhigh` effort level (between `high` and `max`, tuned for tasks over 30 minutes with million-token budgets); high-resolution image input up to 2576 pixels on the long edge; task budgets in beta (advisory token budgets for the full agentic loop). Launched on Amazon Bedrock in 27 AWS regions simultaneously.

### Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026)

- **1M token context window by default** on Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, and Vertex AI (200K on Microsoft Foundry)
- **128K max output tokens**
- Adaptive thinking triggers reasoning only when a turn requires it, reducing wasted tokens vs. Opus 4.7 at the same effort level
- Prompt caching minimum dropped to 1,024 tokens (down from ~2,048)
- Effort parameter defaults to `high` across all surfaces, including Claude Code and the Messages API
- **Mid-conversation system messages**: `role: "system"` messages can appear after a user turn in the `messages` array, preserving cache hits when instructions change mid-session
- Sampling parameters (`temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`) are not supported at non-default values — setting them returns a 400 error

---

## The Fable Tier (June 2026)

On June 9, 2026, Anthropic launched a new model tier above Opus:

- **Claude Fable 5** (`claude-fable-5`) — most capable widely released model
- **Claude Mythos 5** (`claude-mythos-5`) — gated access for Project Glasswing defensive cybersecurity research

Both models: 1M context window by default, 128K max output, always-on adaptive thinking only (manual budget controls removed), and the Opus 4.7 tokenizer (~30% more tokens for the same text).

Fable 5 requires 30-day data retention and is not available under zero data retention contracts. An export-control directive on June 12, 2026 briefly suspended access to both models globally; partial access has been restored for US customers. See [Claude Fable 5 & the Mythos Tier](claude-fable-5-mythos) for the full technical breakdown.

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K → 1M tokens
- **Max output:** ~4K → 8K → 128K tokens
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use → High-resolution vision
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus) → Four tiers (+ Fable/Mythos)
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, managed agent harnesses, long-horizon tasks, and persistent memory across sessions
